extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a new benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in 102 languages. It covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson
extraction.publisher: Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI
extraction.inLanguage: af, am, ar, hy, as, az, be, bn, bs, bg, my, ca, hr, cs, da, nl, en, et, tl, fi, fr, ff, gl, lg, ka, de, el, gu, ha, he, hi, hu, is, ig, id, ga, it, ja, jv, kn, kk, km, ko, ky, lo, lv, ln, lt, mk, ms, ml, mt, mi, mr, mn, ne, nb, ny, oc, or, om, ps, fa, pl, pt, pa, ro, ru, sr, sn, sd, sk, sl, so, es, sw, sv, tg, ta, te, th, tr, uk, ur, uz, vi, cy, wo, xh, yo, zu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark groups several existing multilingual speech datasets (MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14) and introduces a new dataset, Fleurs, for which recordings were collected based on the FLoRes machine translation benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Missing recordings or low-quality recordings are acknowledged and may be replaced in future versions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read audiobooks from Librivox (MLS), European Parliament sessions (VoxPopuli), FLoRes machine translation benchmark sentences (Fleurs), e-banking domain spoken data (Minds-14), and Wikipedia/CommonCrawl text.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Fleurs, new train-dev-test splits were built with 1509, 150, and 350 sentences respectively. For Minds-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the speech retrieval task, the pool of transcription candidates is augmented with 100k sentences from Wikipedia for each language.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For the Fleurs dataset, 2009 n-way parallel sentences were taken from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets, and between one and three speech recordings were collected for each sentence.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Between one and three recordings for each sentence (2.3 on average)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Updates and improvements (e.g., fixing missing or low-quality recordings) will be made on the HuggingFace platform for a second version of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to make speech technology available in all languages, giving speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet and allowing their content and culture to be known outside their language cluster.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: There is a performance discrepancy between geographical language groups, with Western European languages performing much better than Sub-Saharan African or South Asian languages, partly due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data available for Western European languages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Speech classification tasks in the benchmark are prone to overfitting due to the discrepancy between the richness of the input signal (speaker, domain, recording conditions) and the small number of output labels.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of cross-lingual transfer learning, speech recognition, speech-to-text translation, speech classification, and speech retrieval. Practitioners are expected to perform hyperparameter search on the dev set and report performance on the test set.
